headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Devin’s broad write/network/MCP access can conflict with Airflow’s automation outputs, creating default-path data leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can emit task outputs that Devin may ingest through shared integrations or files, and Devin’s MCP/browser/shell stack can parse untrusted content as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is not high, but the interaction pathway is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Airflow task output is copied into Devin’s workspace or an integrated ticket/chat thread
IF Devin treats retrieved file or MCP content as actionable instructions
mitigations: Add a manual review step before Devin acts on Airflow-generated text
Restrict Devin MCP sources to trusted namespaces
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from retrieved artifacts
Tag Airflow outputs as data-only in shared tickets
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between Airflow and Devin

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, while Devin reads and writes cloud workspace files and sends data to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion/MCP integrations. Even though Airflow’s touched data classes are unspecified, shared workspace or ticket handoff can leak file contents or logs into Devin’s outbound channels.
conditions: IF Airflow artifacts are placed in a shared repo, ticket, or Slack thread
IF Devin is allowed to sync those artifacts to GitHub, Slack, Jira, or Notion
mitigations: Keep Airflow outputs in a separate workspace from Devin
Disable Devin write access to Slack/Jira/Notion for shared artifacts
Redact secrets before handing Airflow logs to Devin
Limit Airflow network destinations to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared integrations

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run parallel sessions; Airflow is an automation/orchestration system with broad network egress. In a shared repo or workspace, both can mutate the same artifacts without locking, so default collaboration can overwrite or race changes.
conditions: IF Airflow and Devin target the same repository or workspace path
IF no external lock or branch protection is enforced
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent
Require branch protection and PR review
Assign non-overlapping directories to each agent
Pause one agent while the other writes shared state
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate pipeline facts and artifacts that Devin may treat as authoritative when acting in GitHub, Slack, Jira, or Notion. Because Devin has write authority, a mistaken Airflow output can cascade into commits, tickets, or messages without a verification gate.
conditions: IF Devin consumes Airflow-produced summaries or logs as source of truth
IF Devin is permitted to take downstream actions from those summaries
mitigations: Require Devin to verify Airflow outputs against source data
Block auto-commit from Airflow-derived artifacts
Use checksum or schema validation before actioning outputs
Route high-impact actions to human approval
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware verification

E_compliance.rationale: Devin explicitly handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs with write scopes, while Airflow’s network egress and API calls can move operational data across systems. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch, but differing retention and logging practices across these surfaces create a plausible compliance gap.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive data is placed into Devin-managed integrations
IF Airflow logs or artifacts are retained longer than the source system policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared integrations
Set short retention on Slack/Jira/Notion artifacts
Review Airflow and Devin logging settings
Restrict write scopes to the minimum needed
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion workflows
